record.original_question: Fix m >= 0 and let d = ceil(log_3 m). For n >= d, is the maximum number of affine lines contained in a set of m points in F_3^n always equal to the maximum number of lines achievable by m points already lying in F_3^d? Equivalently, when maximizing lines, is it always optimal to compress the configuration into the smallest possible ambient dimension?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2012.1. Fix m ≥ 0 and let d = ⌈log3(m)⌉. For any n ≥ d, the maximum number of lines contained among m points in Fn3 is equal to the maximum number of lines contained among m points in Fd3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}_3 = \{0,1,2\}$ denote the field with three elements. An (affine) line in $\mathbb{F}_3^n$ is a set of three distinct points $\{x,y,z\} \subset \mathbb{F}_3^n$ satisfying $x+y+z = 0$ (equivalently, three points in arithmetic progression in $\mathbb{F}_3^n$). For integers $m \ge 0$ and $n \ge 1$, define
$$L(m,n) = \max\{\,\#\{\text{lines } \ell \subset S\} : S \subseteq \mathbb{F}_3^n,\ |S| = m\,\},$$
the maximum number of lines that can be contained in an $m$-point subset of $\mathbb{F}_3^n$.

Set $d = \lceil \log_3 m \rceil$, so $d$ is the smallest nonnegative integer with $3^d \ge m$. Prove or disprove: for every $m \ge 0$ and every $n \ge d$,
$$L(m,n) = L(m,d).$$
In words: when maximizing the number of affine lines among $m$ points, is it always optimal to place the configuration inside the smallest ambient affine space $\mathbb{F}_3^d$ that can hold $m$ points?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search on the maximum number of affine lines in subsets of $\mathbb{F}_3^n$ and on dimension-compression conjectures of this type returned only related but distinct results (cap sets, ordinary lines, the Croot–Lev–Pach / Ellenberg–Gijswijt cap-set bound). No source confirming a proof, disproof, or partial resolution of this specific compression-to-minimal-dimension conjecture was found, so its current status could not be verified.

status_evidence.title: Cap set - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: A cap set is a subset of F_3^n in which no three elements sum to zero; bounds on its size are central to extremal questions about lines in F_3^n.
status_evidence.claim: Provides background on lines (3-term APs) in F_3^n but does not address the stated compression conjecture.

status_evidence.title: New Lower Bounds for Cap Sets (arXiv:2209.10045)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent advances on extremal subsets of F_3^n avoiding lines, but no statement on maximizing lines among m points and dimension compression.
status_evidence.claim: Related extremal work on F_3^n does not resolve the conjecture.
